summary: Burlingame sits on a narrow strip of land between the San Francisco Bay and the wooded ridgeline of the Coast Range foothills, and that compressed geography means you can walk from a flat, tree-lined downtown avenue to hillside streets with panoramic bay views in under fifteen minutes. The city's Broadway and Burlingame Avenue corridors function as genuine pedestrian commercial streets — dense with sit-down restaurants, independent coffee shops, and specialty retail. SFO airport lies immediately to the north, which is either a gift (short cab rides before flights) or a nuisance (flight paths overhead), and Caltrain provides a direct rail commute to San Francisco or down to San Jose's tech campuses. The economic math, though, is stark: a median home price exceeding $2 million against a median household income of roughly $169,000 yields a price-to-income ratio above 11, meaning even high earners face significant leverage to buy. Daily highs averaging 66°F year-round with nearly nine hours of sunshine create a mild, fog-moderated climate where seasons register as subtle shifts rather than dramatic swings. Burlingame is essentially a walkable small town grafted onto one of the most expensive commuter corridors in the country — the charm is real, and so is the price of admission.
